title: Finish 1Password install: local polkit owners and MCP setgid

workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Prior-head migration markers prevent existing users from receiving the new hook
leads.consequence: An existing user who ran migration 1789901000.sh on 3d976934 has a marker and the earlier helper did not install a hook. Upgrading Omarchy to this revision will not rerun that migration, so their installed 1Password still has no /etc/pacman.d/hooks/90-omarchy-1password-finish.hook. A later 1password upgrade resets its packaged policy and MCP mode without a repair until the helper is manually invoked or another migration/installer path executes it. Give hook installation a new migration ID or ship the hook in a package.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus (final-report 3.2); only affects machines dev-linked to unmerged 3d976934, negligible; not published

leads.summary: Active hook is absent from both Omarchy runtime PKGBUILDs
leads.consequence: A package built from this PR will carry the new hook only as an inert source under /usr/share/omarchy/default/ via omarchy-settings. Both runtime PKGBUILDs enumerate just three active /usr/share/libalpm/hooks/*.hook files. On a fresh system the migration is already marked complete, so a direct pacman install of 1password (outside Omarchy's service installer) neither installs nor runs this repair and subsequent upgrades still lack the hook. Either package the active hook with its Exec binary or establish a fresh-install and direct-install trigger in the shipped recipes.

leads.summary: A dangling administrator-managed MCP symlink is still overwritten
leads.consequence: Bash -e follows symlinks and reports a dangling symlink as absent. A locally managed /usr/local/bin/1password-mcp pointing to a temporarily unavailable target enters the ! -e branch and sudo ln -sfn replaces the existing symlink with the 1Password helper. This violates the stated preservation behavior and remains changed on later runs. Check -L before treating a path as absent; preserve/report any non-intended link, dangling or live.
leads.triage: corroborated as behaviour (Opus section 4); Opus judged not a defect; published as a completeness remark under F2

leads.summary: The beta package resets the same paths but does not trigger repair
leads.consequence: The shipped 1password-beta package also builds com.1password.1Password.policy using the build host and installs into /opt/1Password. The migration's /opt directory guard repairs an existing beta install once, but this hook targets only package 1password, so a subsequent 1password-beta upgrade restores the build-host policy without rerunning the helper (and, where its tarball includes MCP, resets its mode too). Omarchy's Quattro upgrade tries to replace beta with stable but explicitly leaves beta in place on a failed replacement. If beta installs should be supported, add the beta package trigger (and test it), otherwise scope the migration to stable.
leads.triage: corroborated (Opus C11); published as additional note

leads.summary: Repeated repair overwrites local pacman-hook changes instead of respecting them
leads.consequence: An administrator editing /etc/pacman.d/hooks/90-omarchy-1password-finish.hook to alter/disable a locally owned rule has their version silently replaced by the stock source on the next helper invocation, including a normal package upgrade that fires the hook. A disabling symlink to /dev/null is also non-regular so the source-present branch attempts to install over it. Pacman's local hook override mechanism is intended for exactly this kind of customization. Either package the hook as a managed file with established override rules or only update identifiable Omarchy-authored copies and report conflicts.
leads.triage: corroborated (Opus H3/H4 runtime); published in N2

leads.summary: Uninstall leaves an orphan repair hook and two unowned MCP symlinks
leads.consequence: After the helper writes /etc/pacman.d/hooks/90-omarchy-1password-finish.hook, /usr/local/bin/1password-mcp, and /opt/1Password/onepassword-mcp, the service remover removes only the Chromium extension and the two packages. Pacman does not delete unowned links, and it keeps /opt/1Password when its directory contains the alias. A user still sees a broken MCP executable and a leftover 1Password directory after removal; on a later 1password install when omarchy has also been removed, the stale hook logs an unsatisfied Depends error but cannot execute its /usr/bin target. Cleanup should remove only known helper-owned symlinks/hook and avoid deleting user overrides.
leads.triage: corroborated (Opus E8, 3.4); lifecycle part published in N2; MCP link leftovers kept in local report only

leads.summary: Empty owner input aborts before hook registration and even bypasses its own diagnostic
leads.consequence: On a machine with no four-digit UID in /etc/passwd (for example, a package installed before creating a human account), policy_owners' grep returns 1. With set -euo pipefail the owners=$(policy_owners) assignment fails before the helper's intended 'no four-digit UID users' diagnostic or ensure_upgrade_hook runs. The service installer exits before its Chromium extension and launch (set -e), or a pacman PostTransaction hook logs a failure while leaving the packaged owner and MCP mode unrestored. If a human user is created later, that initial repair did not install the hook to retry. Register the hook independently of policy-owner availability and make the empty owner failure explicit.
leads.triage: corroborated (Opus E1); published as additional note

leads.summary: Package-hook coverage test does not enumerate the new active hook
leads.consequence: The packaging contract test checks that omarchy PKGBUILD explicitly installs each of three hard-coded hook files but never names 90-omarchy-1password-finish.hook. Accordingly config-test passes with both runtime package recipes missing this new hook, masking REG. Add the fourth entry (or derive the list from default/libalpm/hooks/ with an explicit exclusion for intentionally local-only hooks).
leads.triage: corroborated (Opus 6: config-test does not list hook); folded into N2 suggested change

leads.summary: Changed test passes when its installed hook is changed to PreTransaction
leads.consequence: The new test verifies only that the hook file exists and contains Target = 1password and the helper name. A plausible regression changing When to PreTransaction would run repair before pacman replaces the packaged policy and MCP binary, so F1 recurs, but the whole fixture still passes. Assert When = PostTransaction and, preferably, emulate a package overwrite followed by hook execution. This is a test-gap lead, not evidence that the shipped PostTransaction hook is wrong.
leads.triage: factual: coordinator read test lines (only Target/helper-name greps); Opus self-check run review-plan-3/20260927T150704Z-f2371f75 confirmed mutant passes; published as Optional test improvement

leads.summary: Two live 1Password installer PRs require an explicit combined hunk
leads.consequence: #9024 adds the allowed-browsers scaffold at the exact insertion site of this PR's finish call, and #8575 changes this PR's 1Password launch command. Both heads diverge from this PR, and merge-file using each PR's true merge-base leaves conflict markers in the installer (#9024 at merged/pr-9024.merged:27-35, #8575 at merged/pr-8575.merged:43-47). When resolving, keep both the finish call and browser scaffolding for #9024, and preserve setsid plus the intended GSETTINGS_BACKEND=memory environment for #8575; merely taking either conflicting side drops the other's behavior. This is an integration heads-up, not a claim the two PRs have merged.
leads.triage: #9024 corroborated by Opus (trivial text conflict); #8575 not independently checked; routine text conflicts omitted from public comment as low value

issues.requirement: Substantive findings need descriptive headings, observed behavior, Impact and Suggested change. Compact labelled paragraphs are for brief test or documentation notes. Avoid invented severity labels.
issues.excerpt: **Minor notes:** ... `owners=$(policy_owners)` fails under `set -euo pipefail`. The helper exits 1 before printing its own diagnostic and before installing the hook. ... The hook targets only `1password`. ... so beta upgrades do not trigger the repair.
issues.correction: Two of these notes describe production behavior: the helper exits early without installing the hook, and beta upgrades skip the repair. Neither is a test or documentation note, and neither states an actionable correction. The 'Minor' label also acts as an unexplained severity qualifier. Give each production note a one-line Suggested change, such as handling an empty owner list with a diagnostic, or also targeting `1password-beta`, and replace 'Minor notes' with a neutral label such as 'Additional notes'. If the coordinator judges either note substantive, promote it to a headed finding with Impact and Suggested change. The migration file-mode note already implies its correction (`0644`) and can stay as one sentence. Whether each note is substantive is a technical judgment for the coordinator; this issue concerns presentation only.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to [the earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12715#issuecomment-5789025102) and [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12715#issuecomment-5841759326), checked at `e57f217dacc3`. **Verified:** both earlier findings are resolved at this revision. Two further points concern packaging: the repair conflicts with two open package-side fixes in `omacom/omarchy-pkgs`, which the new hook makes recur after each upgrade, and the hook is installed differently from Omarchy's other pacman hooks.

| Earlier finding | At `e57f217dacc3` |
|---|---|
| Package upgrades undo the repair | Resolved |
| Existing local MCP command replaced | Resolved |

**Verified (upgrades):** the helper now installs `/etc/pacman.d/hooks/90-omarchy-1password-finish.hook`, a `PostTransaction` hook for Install and Upgrade of `1password` that re-runs the helper. In pacman's source, PostTransaction hooks run after the package's own install scriptlets, and a failing PostTransaction hook cannot abort the transaction. In an isolated simulated hook run after a simulated upgrade (build-host owner restored, MCP binary without setgid), the helper restored local owners and issued `chgrp onepassword-mcp` and `chmod g+s` again.

**Verified (local MCP command):** each existing-path case for `/usr/local/bin/1password-mcp` was run against both revisions in isolated fixtures:

| Existing path | `3d976934ba27` | `e57f217dacc3` |
|---|---|---|
| Regular file (local wrapper) | Replaced | Kept, message printed |
| Symlink to another existing file or directory | Replaced | Kept, message printed |
| Directory | Link created inside it | Kept, message printed |
| Symlink already pointing to the helper | Re-created | Kept, no change |
| Absent, or dangling symlink | Link created | Link created |

The dangling-symlink row still replaces an entry that does not resolve. This refreshes stale links from earlier installs and is noted only for completeness.

### Conflicts with open package fixes omarchy-pkgs#442 and #489

Two open `omarchy-pkgs` PRs fix the same issues on the package side, and this helper works against both:

- [omarchy-pkgs#442](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy-pkgs/pull/442) packages `/opt/1Password/onepassword-mcp` as a symlink. This helper creates that same path as an unowned symlink when it is absent (already the case at `3d976934ba27`). pacman's file-conflict check rejects a new package file that already exists on disk unowned unless `--overwrite` matches it, and `bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs` passes only `--overwrite '/usr/share/omarchy/*'`. The automatic conflict handler in `bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs-when-conflicted` clears unowned paths only for conflicts reported against the `omarchy` packages, so it does not cover this one.
- [omarchy-pkgs#489](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy-pkgs/pull/489) ships a static `unix-group:wheel` policy owner. The helper replaces any existing owner value. An isolated run confirmed `unix-group:wheel` is rewritten to the local user list, and the new hook would repeat that after every 1Password upgrade.

```text
helper has run  -> /opt/1Password/onepassword-mcp exists, owned by no package
upgrade to #442 -> package ships the same path -> "exists in filesystem" conflict
#489 installed  -> policy owner unix-group:wheel -> hook rewrites to unix-user:... after each upgrade
```

**Impact:** On systems this helper has repaired, an `omarchy update` to a package built from #442 would stop with a file conflict until the alias is removed. This is from pacman and PR source, not an executed upgrade. If #489 lands, the hook overrides the package's chosen policy owner after every 1Password install or upgrade on systems where the hook exists.

**Suggested change:** Decide between the Omarchy-side repair and the package fixes, or sequence them. Options on this side: drop the `/opt/1Password/onepassword-mcp` alias, or remove it in the same change that adopts #442. Limit the owner rewrite to unresolved templates and owner entries that name no local account (such as `unix-user:builder`), so a package-shipped group owner is kept.

### Repair hook is copied into /etc instead of shipped with the package

Omarchy ships its alpm hooks as package-owned files under `/usr/share/libalpm/hooks` through the `omarchy` PKGBUILD (with a comment about avoiding package skew), and `test/shell.d/config-test.sh` checks that pairing for the hooks it lists. The new hook source sits in `default/libalpm/hooks/`, but only the helper copies it into `/etc/pacman.d/hooks`, the administrator's hook directory.

**Impact:**
- The hook exists only after the helper has run once. The `omarchy` package pre-seeds migration markers for new users, so on systems installed from a release that already contains this migration, installing 1Password with `omarchy pkg add` or `pacman -S` (rather than the service installer) gets neither the repair nor the hook. The same applies to existing systems where the migration ran before 1Password was installed, because it is marked done even when `/opt/1Password` is absent.
- The `/etc` copy is not removed with `omarchy` or 1Password. Retiring it later needs a migration.
- Whenever the helper runs, it overwrites an administrator-edited copy, and replaces a `/dev/null` mask (the documented way to disable a hook) with the stock file (both seen in isolated runs).

**Suggested change:** Ship the hook package-owned through the `omarchy` PKGBUILD with a companion `omarchy-pkgs` change, as open PR #11097 does for its hook, and add it to the hook list in `config-test.sh`. If the `/etc` copy stays, leave a `/dev/null` mask alone, replace a differing copy only when it matches a previously shipped version, and report anything else, as the MCP link logic now does.

**Additional notes:**
- `migrations/1789901000.sh` is committed as mode `100755`. `agents/skills/migrations.md` requires `0644`, which every other migration uses. Suggested change: commit it as `0644`.
- With no four-digit-UID users, `owners=$(policy_owners)` fails under `set -euo pipefail`. The helper exits 1 before printing its own diagnostic and before installing the hook. Suggested change: handle an empty owner list explicitly so the diagnostic prints, and install the hook before the owner rewrite.
- The hook targets only `1password`. `omarchy-pkgs` also ships `1password-beta` with the same build-time owner expansion, so beta upgrades do not trigger the repair. Suggested change: add `Target = 1password-beta`, or scope the migration to the stable package.

**Optional test improvement:** the hook assertions check only that the file exists and contains `Target = 1password` and the helper name. A mutant with `When = PreTransaction`, which would reapply the repair before pacman replaces the files, still passes. Asserting `When = PostTransaction` closes that gap.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned source at `e57f217dacc3` and `3d976934ba27`, `omarchy-pkgs` packaging at `93c13910e3c0` including open PRs #442 and #489, and pacman v7.1.0 source. The repository test ran in an isolated sandbox: it passes at the head and on a trial merge with the current `quattro` tip, and fails with the `3d976934ba27` helper. Helper branches ran in isolated fixtures with stubbed `sudo` and synthetic users. No real pacman transaction, polkit authorization, MCP authentication or real root run was tested.

**AI process:** Fresh follow-up review: Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
